title: Seqlock fallback recreates torn-down resources from a stale snapshot; neural_fmt is never reconciled afterwards
failure_scenario: Panel open, user toggles 'HDR codec' ON->OFF (a_teardown at k_rebuild). The service releases the feature and textures and opens the rebuild gate. The first accepted dispatch after the gate opens overlaps that frame's draw_controls on the present thread - ui_seq is held ODD for the whole of draw_controls (overlay_ui.hpp:2529-2546) while begin_pass's 8-attempt seqlock loop spins in nanoseconds with no backoff - so begin_pass takes the !snapshot_ok fallback (overlay_ui.hpp:1103-1115) and returns true with the PREVIOUS g_cfg (hdr_codec still 1). nr_ensure_output's create branch (stray_dlssnr.cpp:2636) then creates out_tex r16g16b16a16_float against the stale value. The next pass commits hdr_codec=0, hits the fast path (w/h/out_fmt unchanged, :2600-2607), and no code path ever re-checks neural_fmt against the current hdr_codec - unlike every other create-latched key (feature_matches, key_moved/geometry_moved). Result: the codec-off copy-back is skipped EVERY frame (src_fmt=neural_fmt != taa_out.fmt, :6175) - silent permanent loss of the denoise until the next teardown, with one LOGE (:6186-6193) whose explanation names the wrong cause. The OFF->ON direction symmetrically yields an r11g11b10 neural target under a running codec - the state :2537-2543 logs as 'This should be impossible' - a persistent per-pixel quantisation floor. This is exactly the hazard the control's own comment (overlay_ui.hpp:3145-3152) says the teardown exists to prevent; the fallback path re-opens it, with roughly draw_controls-duration/frame-time odds per toggle.
fix: Give the codec/neural-format pairing the same self-correcting per-pass seam every other create-latched key has: in nr_ensure_output's fast path, when out_tex exists, also verify (g_cfg.hdr_codec && st.codec.ok && !st.codec_failed) == (st.neural_fmt == r16g16b16a16_float) (for out_fmt != FP16) and on disagreement fetch_or(kTeardown) and return false, exactly as the resolution-change branch above it does. Alternatively (or additionally), make begin_pass's !snapshot_ok fallback return false instead of true - the comment's 'a dropped denoise frame' cost argument does not survive the create-after-teardown case.

title: sr_latched_off / chain_nr_off are permanent, invisible, and unclearable while every control reports success
failure_scenario: The user pins sr_out_width/height (or another evaluate-affecting SR setting) wrongly; EvaluateFeature fails 8 consecutive frames (~130ms) and sr_latched_off latches. The user then fixes the pin in the overlay: the service reports 'reconfigure APPLIED', the panel's SR line shows green 'DLSS-SR is ARMED - the branch is live now' (overlay_ui.hpp:3274), and 'Reset NR feature' - whose tooltip says it is 'the control to reach for when something has wedged' - clears only feature_failed (stray_dlssnr.cpp:7393). But sr_try_run bails on st.sr_latched_off at :3795 forever, the SR_BAIL one-shot was burnt when the latch first fired, so every later frame silently runs no SR at all until relaunch. Nothing publishes sr_latched_off to the overlay, no reconfigure bit clears it, and the deliberate-latch comments (:2342, :2306) only argue the resolution-change case, not user reconfigures. chain_nr_off has the identical shape. The 'deliberately not cleared' rationale (NGX refused something intrinsic) is false for evaluate failures caused by panel-tunable parameters that the panel exists to fix.
fix: Clear sr_latched_off, sr_mvec_rejected, chain_nr_off and mvec_eval_rejected (and their streak counters) in the a_clear_failed arm of nr_service_reconfigure, so 'Reset NR feature' honours its tooltip; additionally publish sr_latched_off to the overlay so the SR status line can say LATCHED OFF instead of 'the branch is live now'.

title: draw_status has no rung for the SR configurations and misdiagnoses both in red
failure_scenario: Pure-SR run (dlss_nr=0, dlss_sr=1, enabled=1 - the configuration the three-scope fix at :2560 was made for): nvngx_dlssnr.dll is deliberately never loaded, so f.snippet_loaded is false and the status headline is red 'WAITING FOR NGX - the snippet is not loaded' with the fallback 'nvngx_dlssnr.dll could not be loaded (no reason was recorded)' - a load failure that never happened. Worse, at the shipped default require_trampoline=1 the next line claims 'remix_nvngx.dll is required ... and was not found beside the add-on' (:2356) while remix_nvngx.dll was found and is actively carrying every SR call through slot B - f.trampoline reads only g_snippet (stray_dlssnr.cpp:8119), never g_sr_snippet. The red misdiagnosis sits directly above a green 'DLSS-SR is ARMED'. Second config, dlss_nr=1 + dlss_sr=1 (documented: 'DLSS-SR TAKES the dispatch. With this on, the DLSS-NR evaluate does not run'): begin_pass stamps pass_seen_ms every accepted dispatch but publish_evaluate is never called on the plain-SR branch, so the headline is permanently red 'NOT EVALUATING - the TAA pass is reached but no evaluate has succeeded' (:2445) while DLSS-SR evaluates every frame.
fix: Add a dlss_nr=0 rung to draw_status ('DLSS-NR is off by configuration; see the DLSS-SR section') before the snippet_loaded check, derive the trampoline fact from either snippet (g_snippet OR g_sr_snippet), and gate the evals==0 red rung on the dispatch actually being routed to the NR evaluate (not when live_dlss_sr() has taken it).

title: out_tex create_resource failure has no per-resolution latch and its LOGE fires every frame
failure_scenario: create_resource for the output texture fails (VRAM exhaustion - the exact 4K scenario dlss_sr's own out_failed message names as 'the first place a memory problem shows up'). nr_ensure_output logs an UNGATED LOGE and returns false with no latch set; out_tex stays 0, so the next accepted dispatch re-enters the create branch, attempts the allocation again, fails again, and logs again - one ERROR line plus one failed create_resource per frame (60+/s), with ReShade flushing the log per message, for as long as the pressure lasts. Every comparable allocation in this codebase (codec_tex_failed, orig_failed, mvec_tex_failed, feature_failed, dlss_sr::out_failed) carries a per-resolution latch documented as existing precisely because 'retrying it every frame would be a per-frame allocation attempt on the hot path' and because unguarded messages 'would otherwise be printed on every single frame' (:1653). The most important allocation of all is the one without either.
fix: Add an out_tex_failed per-(w,h,fmt) latch in nr_state, set it on this failure path, test it at the top of nr_ensure_output's create branch, clear it in nr_release_feature_and_output alongside codec_tex_failed, and gate the LOGE behind the existing one-shot pattern.

title: dlss_nr=0 + dlss_chain=1 falls through to the DLSS-NR takeover with no parameter block: silent per-frame takeover that can never evaluate, while the fallback log claims the game is untouched
failure_scenario: Set dlss_nr=0, dlss_sr=0, dlss_chain=1 (sr_shader_hash=0 as shipped, game in the normal non-upsampling TAA config). The SR snippet loads and arms (the load gate at :6376 ORs dlss_chain in), so g_nr_armed is true and the nr_state guard at :4860 passes because sr_feat.params is non-null. chain_ok (:5038) is false because st->params is null, and dlss_sr is 0, so the branch at :5239 is NOT taken and control falls into the DLSS-NR path with st->params == nullptr. want_hash falls back to shader_hash, u0 is at the colour extent, so the pass proceeds all the way: it allocates the FP16 output texture plus aux textures, takes the pre-denoise full-res copy and records the mvec-decode dispatch every frame (the shared pipeline is built because sr_mvec_decode gates OR dlss_chain, :6618), captures and replays the full root state, RE-ISSUES the game's dispatch (issued=true, so co-loaded add-ons never see the event), and then nr_ensure_feature returns false silently every frame at :2684 — no log, no latch, no possible evaluate, forever. Meanwhile the one diagnostic that fires (:5053) asserts the run "falls back to the game's own TAA, untouched". In the documented chain setup (MainUpsampling + sr_shader_hash pinned) the same hole surfaces differently: sr_out_w is 0 because chain_ok is false, the DLSS-NR extent rule rejects the 4K u0, and the user gets the misdirecting error "the configured output register u0 is not a usable TAA output" telling them to change uav_output, when the actual cause is dlss_nr=0.
fix: Before the takeover, bail on the DLSS-NR path when st->params == nullptr — e.g. after the SR branch at :5239, `if (st->params == nullptr) NR_BAIL("dlss_nr=0: the DLSS-NR parameter block was never allocated, and neither dlss_sr nor a runnable chain claimed this dispatch")` — so the fail-open contract's strict no-op actually holds; and make the :5042 chain-unavailable message name this state instead of claiming the game is untouched.

title: sr_suppress_taa=1 + sr_direct_output=1: no UAV barrier between NGX's writes to u0 and the TAAU dispatch ReShade re-issues on the failure path — the ladder's 'TAAU overwrites the partial work' claim assumes an ordering D3D12 does not provide
failure_scenario: Under suppress+direct, when EvaluateFeature fails after recording partial UAV writes to taa_out (the contract comment at :3689-3696 explicitly relies on "that shader ... overwrites whatever partial work we recorded"), sr_try_run leaves issued=false and returns; ReShade then issues the game's TAAU dispatch directly. Between NGX's recorded UAV writes to u0 and that re-issued dispatch's UAV writes there is no barrier of any kind on taa_out — the closing section (:4640-4683) barriers only the add-on's own textures, and the one UAV barrier on taa_out (:4260) is on the non-suppress path. Two unordered UAV-state writes to the same resource may interleave on the GPU, so the "CORRECT frame" the fallback promises can be a torn mix of NGX's partial output and TAAU's for that frame (vkd3d-proton will not diagnose it). The same gap covers an exception unwinding after NGX recorded work. If, conversely, EvaluateFeature never records work before failing, the race cannot occur — but then the load-bearing "partial work is overwritten" comment describes a mechanism that does not exist; either way code and comment disagree with D3D12's rules.
fix: On the suppress && direct && !evaluated path, record one `cmd->barrier(taa_out.res, unordered_access, unordered_access)` before returning (ReShade turns the matching UA pair into a real UAV barrier, per the :4255 comment), so anything NGX recorded is ordered before the re-issued TAAU; or establish that a failed EvaluateFeature records nothing and rewrite the contract comment to say that instead.

title: Chain give-up latch does not cover CreateFeature failure: a latched NR create failure leaves the codec encode dispatch running every frame forever, with output nothing reads
failure_scenario: Chain mode with hdr_codec on: if CreateFeature(feature 18) fails at the render extent (e.g. FAIL_OutOfGPUMemory at :2711), st.feature_failed latches and nr_ensure_feature short-circuits false every frame thereafter (:2682). But nr_codec_encode at :4351 runs BEFORE nr_ensure_feature and is gated only on chain_codec, and chain_nr_fail_streak is incremented only inside the ngx::failed(nr_r) branch (:4406) which is inside `if (nr_ensure_feature(...))` — so chain_nr_off (the latch whose own message says paying "for an encode ... every frame for an answer nothing can use is not something to do silently") can never latch on a create failure. Result: a full-render-extent encode dispatch plus its proxy barriers are recorded every frame for the rest of the run, the proxy is never read (decode and the NR evaluate are both skipped), and after the two one-shot logs (create-fail, chain-sr-only) the cost is permanent and silent. The frame itself stays correct (DLSS-SR alone).
fix: Fold the create failure into the chain gate: skip the encode when st.feature_failed (move the nr_ensure_feature call, or its failure test, above the chain_codec block), or count a nr_ensure_feature false toward chain_nr_fail_streak so chain_nr_off latches on it the same way it does for evaluate failures.

title: Per-key ladder table and three live_block declaration comments describe SR create-key wiring the code no longer has
failure_scenario: The authoritative PER KEY table (overlay_ui.hpp:145-151) states 'nothing in the render path compares them against what the live feature was created with. The "Recreate the SR feature" button is the mechanism and every tooltip says so' - the exact sentence the control-site comment at :3489-3491 certifies as false ('that was false in this tree even then'): the create-param latch (stray_dlssnr.cpp:3989-4046, feature_matches) compares create_flags, hw_depth and perf_quality and queues kTeardown itself, and the tooltips now say 'no button needed'. Three declaration comments repeat the stale wiring: :416 claims sr_perf_quality/sr_render_preset 'raise a_teardown' (both are wired k_plain with zero bits, :3356/:3365); :444 claims tier-1 flags 'point at the recreate button' (they auto-rebuild); :455 claims tier-2 extent keys raise 'a_teardown | a_reconcile at k_rebuild' (actual: k_reset, zero bits, the geometry test queues kTeardown, :3460-3464). The biting direction is sr_render_preset: a maintainer trusting :416 concludes a preset change takes effect automatically, but feature_matches deliberately skips preset (stray_dlssnr.cpp:4014-4015) and only the recreate button applies it - the next reader builds a control on a teardown that never happens.
fix: Rewrite the CREATE entry at :145-151 and the declaration comments at :414-418, :441-444 and :453-455 to match the control-site comments: flags/hw_depth/perf_quality auto-rebuild via the create-param latch; sr_render_preset alone is button-only; tier-2 extents are k_reset + geometry-detected.

title: DLSS-NR ARMED banner prints ~15 live keys from g_cfg, misreporting pre-arm panel edits
failure_scenario: The 'tuning', 'behaviour', 'hdr codec' (paper_white_scale/transfer_strength/color_strength), 'mvec decode' (mvec_dilate/clip_row/transpose/scales) and 'feedback fix' banner lines (stray_dlssnr.cpp:6880-6908) read g_cfg, but every key they print is in OVERLAY_OWNED_FIELDS and the per-pass snapshot, and the banner runs above begin_pass - so g_cfg still holds the ini's values. Concrete case (the one the neighbouring comments at :6863-6875 name as the reason the identification block was fixed): enabled=0 at launch, user sets Intensity=0.30 and transfer_strength=0.5 in the panel, ticks enabled - the arm banner, the bring-up instrument, reports Intensity=1.000 transfer_strength=1.000 while the first evaluate uses the edited values. The SR banner was swept for exactly this defect (:6768-6781, 'seventeen keys ... were still being printed from g_cfg') and the NR banner's identification and hdr_codec/mvec gate flags were converted; these five lines were missed. Log-only lie, no data race (same thread, pre-snapshot).
fix: Read the overlay's atomics for the live keys on these five lines, exactly as the identification block above them and the SR banner already do (one live_block reference, relaxed loads); keep g_cfg only for app_id and other genuinely load-only values.

title: reconfig_pending is cleared while requeued work is still outstanding during an in-flight init
failure_scenario: The in-flight branch (stray_dlssnr.cpp:7255-7272) deliberately returns without clearing reconfig_pending ('REBUILDING is exactly what is happening') after requeuing the drained bits into st_raw->pending_work - which is only drained once init_complete is stored. But the very next present takes the work==0 early exit (:7127-7131) and stores reconfig_pending=false, because the queued work is invisible from there (pending_work is only merged when st != nullptr, :7124-7125). Scenario: dlss_nr=1, enabled=0 at launch; user ticks enabled (arm) then ticks HDR codec during nr_lazy_ngx_init's several hundred milliseconds - the panel's REBUILDING rung shows for one present, goes dark for the rest of the init while the teardown and codec build are still owed, then reappears when init settles. This violates the field's stated contract (overlay_ui.hpp:646-650: 'Set by the service while work is outstanding and cleared when it has all been done') - the two branches disagree about who owns the flag during init.
fix: In the work==0 early exit, keep reconfig_pending true when st_raw exists, g_nr_init_settled is false and st_raw->pending_work.load() != 0 (the same three facts the in-flight branch already establishes); or, if the flicker is judged acceptable, amend the in-flight branch's comment and the reconfig_pending declaration so they no longer promise a guarantee the code does not keep.

title: SR guide-revert rung tests streak == 3 on a counter that increments regardless of mvec_used, so it can be skipped permanently
failure_scenario: sr_eval_fail_streak is incremented unconditionally at :4530 on every failed evaluate, including frames where the decoded guide was not bound (mvec_used false - clip_ok flapping, a transient ensure_mvec failure, or the user ticking sr_mvec_decode on mid-failure). The revert rung fires only at the exact equality streak == 3 with mvec_used true. If the streak passes 3 on a raw-guide frame and the decoded guide comes back on frame 4-7, the equality never matches again: the run skips the 'give the raw guide back' rung entirely and goes straight to sr_latched_off at 8 - landing on 'no SR at all' where the ladder's contract says every rung lands on today's behaviour. The DLSS-NR analogue at :5885 is immune: its increment is gated on mvec_used and its threshold is >= 8.
fix: Mirror the NR shape: keep a separate mvec-attributed streak (increment only when mvec_used, reset on success) and trigger the revert on >= 3 rather than == 3.

title: Teardown re-arm list omits all seven chain one-shots; logged_chain_out_fail is burnt by the benign geometry-move path
failure_scenario: The R3 block ('Let every one-shot diagnostic speak again for the new configuration') re-arms the NR, mvec, hist and SR one-shots but none of logged_chain_unavailable/not_upsampling/codec_off/banner/nr_fail/sr_only/out_fail, and nr_release_feature_and_output clears chain_nr_fail_streak (:2309) without re-arming its paired logged_chain_nr_fail - exactly the pairing defect the SR comment at :2333 names ('clearing the latch while leaving the printed-once flag set would make the retry at the new geometry silent'). Concretely: any mid-run render-resolution change while chained routes through nr_ensure_output's extent-mismatch return at :4161 and burns logged_chain_out_fail on the benign self-healing case; if a REAL allocation failure later occurs at some extent, chain_run silently drops to SR-only every frame for the rest of the session with no chain-level log line, and the per-extent 'could not be allocated at this extent' rung of logged_chain_codec_off likewise never speaks again after its first firing.
fix: Add the seven logged_chain_* flags to the want_teardown re-arm list in nr_service_reconfigure (leaving logged_chain_banner out if a re-print is unwanted), or split logged_chain_out_fail so the geometry-move case does not consume the allocation-failure one-shot.

title: RT census 'COMPILED SET: EMPTY' omits the mid-session-arm cause its own reconfigure ladder made the headline case
failure_scenario: note_pipeline returns immediately while enabled is false, so every RT state object UE compiled before the census was armed is never counted. The reconfigure ladder made mid-session arming via set_live the flagship use ('the case where NGX did NOT arm is exactly when a user wants the shader census turned on'), and UE 4.27 compiles its RT pipelines at startup/level load - so a user who ticks rt_census mid-session gets a summary with dispatches climbing normally but 'COMPILED SET: EMPTY', whose message lists exactly three causes (no RT built, RESHADE_ADDON==1 build, RDAT-stripped libraries) and tells the reader to use the non-zero dispatch count to pick between the last two. The true cause - the census was armed after the pipelines were compiled - is not listed, so the message's own guidance steers the user to a confident wrong diagnosis of their ReShade build.
fix: Record in state whether arming happened after init (set_live vs arm), and have the EMPTY branch name late arming as the first candidate cause when dispatches are non-zero, or state unconditionally that pipelines compiled before arming are invisible.

title: Census camera-cut line reports detector=LIVE forever once jitter validated a single time
failure_scenario: jitter_cut_ok is stored true at :3353 and never cleared anywhere - not by nr_release_feature_and_output, not by a_clear_clip, not when mvec_eval_rejected latches the decode off (after which nr_update_clip_to_prev_clip, which hosts the detector, is never called again). So: decode runs at 1080p with the jitter row validated (detector genuinely LIVE); the resolution changes and the new discovery's jitter row does not validate, or NGX rejects the decoded guide and the decode latches off - cut detection has actually stopped, DLSSNR.Reset is no longer pulsed on cuts, but every periodic census for the rest of the run prints 'detector=LIVE (View.TemporalAAJitter.zw==.xy)'. A player reporting ghosting across cutscene cuts is told by the log that the cut detector is working.
fix: Clear jitter_cut_ok in nr_release_feature_and_output alongside the other per-resolution jitter state, and store false when the decode path stops calling the detector (mvec_eval_rejected / run_mvec == raw), or rename the census wording to 'validated at least once this run'.

title: nr_update_clip_to_prev_clip header contract ('every false path has already logged its reason') is false for two silent permanent latches
failure_scenario: Two paths latch view_layout_failed permanently and log nothing themselves: the discovery bound at :3209 (8 consecutive transient read_view_cb failures) and the row-bounds check at :3339. The caller's generic logged_mvec_off one-shot fires on the FIRST raw frame - typically for the transient reason - so when the permanent latch lands frames later it is indistinguishable in the log from a transient that recovered, and the specific diagnosis (discovery Map failures exhausted the retry budget; the pinned mvec_clip_row is outside the pool) is never printed. A future maintainer reading the header contract at :3140-3141 will assume both paths are covered and build on it, which is the exact comment-drift failure this review brief names.
fix: Add a one-shot LOGW to each of the two silent latch sites (naming discover_tries exhaustion and the out-of-bounds row respectively), or amend the header comment to say which false paths rely on the caller's generic ladder message.

title: Reconfigure log/panel misattributes SR create-param teardowns as a resolution change
failure_scenario: The service's fallback attribution predates the chain/live-settings merges: `from_overlay = (req.bits != 0u) || req.ident_changed` and the else-string "the TAA output resolution or format changed" assume nr_ensure_output is the only bit-less source of kTeardown (the enum comment at :1512 still says "kTeardown is the one bit this file raises on its own, from nr_ensure_output"). sr_try_run now raises kTeardown from three more sites, and the seven SR create-flag checkboxes plus sr_perf_quality are deliberately wired k_plain with no action bits (overlay_ui.hpp ~3460-3520: "the render path notices the change by itself"). Concrete: the user ticks "IsHDR (sr_hdr)" mid-session; the create-param latch at stray_dlssnr.cpp:4032-4046 raises kTeardown with no overlay bits; the next present logs `DLSS-NR reconfigure APPLIED: "the TAA output resolution or format changed" -> tier 1 (feature recreate)` and the panel's REBUILDING rung shows the same text, though no resolution or format moved. Anyone diagnosing from the log or panel concludes a spurious geometry change occurred; the truthful "a CREATE-LATCHED parameter moved" line appears only earlier, in a different log block.
fix: Track which seam raised kTeardown (e.g. a second pending bit or a stored string-literal reason in nr_state written by sr_try_run's three fetch_or sites), and update the enum comment at :1512 to name sr_try_run's three sites alongside nr_ensure_output.

title: slider_u32 comment claims out-of-range values are shown; the code clamps the display
failure_scenario: The comment says "A value outside the range is SHOWN rather than clamped away, on the same argument combo_u32 makes above: ... a widget that silently rewrote it would make the panel disagree with what is actually being matched" — but the next two lines (`if (v < lo) v = lo; if (v > hi) v = hi;`) clamp the displayed value before SliderInt. combo_u32 genuinely implements the promised show-as-is behaviour (amber "not a listed value - sent as-is"); slider_u32 never did. Concrete: stray_dlssnr.ini has srv_colour = 99 (or mvec_clip_row = 600, a deliberate out-of-range pin). The atomic keeps 99/600 and the render path matches t99 / reads row 600, but the panel displays 63 / 511 — exactly the panel-vs-reality disagreement the comment claims to prevent. A user checking the panel against the log sees two different numbers for the same key with no indication which is live.
fix: Either implement the promised behaviour (render the raw number in amber like combo_u32 when v is outside [lo,hi] and skip the slider), or rewrite the comment to say the DISPLAY is clamped while the stored value is preserved.

title: Seven dead one-shot log latches; the service re-arms two of them as if they guarded messages
failure_scenario: dlss_sr::feature declares five latches — logged_first_eval, logged_jitter_zero, logged_no_jitter, logged_out_extent, logged_hw_depth (dlss_sr.hpp:501-505) — with zero readers or writers anywhere in the tree; their real counterparts migrated to nr_state (logged_sr_no_jitter, logged_sr_out_extent) and jitter_source (logged_zero, logged_failed) during the dlss-sr merge, stranding the feature-struct copies. The struct comment above them still promises "the latch is named after the message". Similarly nr_state::logged_mvec_active (stray_dlssnr.cpp:1682) and nr_state::logged_sr_banner (:1894) are never set or tested — yet nr_service_reconfigure's teardown block CLEARS both (:7567, :7587) inside a comment claiming to "let every one-shot diagnostic speak again". Concrete: a maintainer auditing which message each latch guards (the exact audit the struct comments invite) finds seven latches guarding nothing, and the service's re-arm list asserts re-arming effects that do not exist — the same "compiles but never runs" shape this project has already shipped once and documents as its recurring failure mode.
fix: Delete the five dead fields from dlss_sr::feature, delete nr_state::logged_mvec_active and logged_sr_banner, and drop the two corresponding lines from nr_service_reconfigure's re-arm blocks.

title: Bulk of intra-tree line-number citations are stale after the night's merges; several are load-bearing
failure_scenario: Verified-wrong citations, all displaced by the ~2000-line growth of stray_dlssnr.cpp: (a) :6575 says "g_cfg.hdr_codec alone gates the three sites that consult it (:1816, :2043, :3307)" — the real sites are :2367, :2636, :5551, plus a FOURTH the chain merge added at :4192 (so the count is wrong too); the cited lines land on hist_restored atomics, publish_codec_build, and a LOGI continuation. (b) :7071's lock-order proof cites nr_try_run taking st->mutex at :2744 and g.mutex at :2771 — actual :4873/:4914. (c) overlay_ui.hpp's header rules cite ~30 stray_dlssnr.cpp lines (:2201/:2225, :2333/:3033 for the restore_graphics_root tear argument, :1663 :2499 :2636 :2882 :3050 :3069 for copy_back's six sites, :4425/:4430/:4449 for the diagnostics read sites, :4339-4341 for the FreeLibrary refusal — the last also quoted verbatim in two USER-FACING tooltips) — every one lands in unrelated code, while the same header records the lesson "a hook list that names stale lines is worse than one that names none". (d) mvec_decode.hpp cites :1639-1643/:2594-2596 for rules now at ~2340/~5560. Concrete: the next maintainer greps :2333/:3033 to verify the restore_graphics_root corruption argument before making the knob per-frame-atomic, lands in nr_ensure_aux, and — per this tree's own documented failure pattern — re-derives the claim wrong or trusts it blind.
fix: Sweep intra-tree :NNNN citations and replace with symbol names (function + short quoted anchor) rather than line numbers, as the overlay hook list already does; at minimum fix the four load-bearing ones (:6575, :7071, overlay rules 1/3, the two tooltips quoting stray_dlssnr.cpp:4339-4341).

title: Stale section header on sr_try_run: 'Reached ONLY ... when g_cfg.dlss_sr is 1' — chain mode reaches it with dlss_sr=0
failure_scenario: The DLSS-SR section header states "Reached ONLY from nr_try_run, and only when g_cfg.dlss_sr is 1", but the call site at :5239 is `if (g_cfg.dlss_sr || chain_ok)` — dlss_chain=1 with dlss_sr=0 enters this function every accepted dispatch. A reader trusting the header (this codebase's stated norm) would conclude the chain cannot be in play whenever dlss_sr=0 and reason wrongly about which preconditions the shared code above the branch has established — precisely the stale-comment hazard the codebase's own :2578-2584 block exists to prevent.
fix: Update the header to "Reached ONLY from nr_try_run, when g_cfg.dlss_sr is 1 or the chain is runnable (chain_ok)", matching the wording the branch-point comment at :5232-5237 already uses.

title: Coarse-key comment claims 'the finer test still catches' a view-rect-only move, but in the exact configuration the coarse key was added for the finer test is vacuous
failure_scenario: The comment above the coarse geometry key says "render_w below can only differ from colour.w by the view rect, which is a sub-texture refinement of the same movement, and the finer test still catches that." But every clause of the finer geometry_moved test (:3958-3971) requires a live handle or an allocated texture, and the block's own opening paragraph (:3831-3835) establishes that with sr_direct_output=1 and no mvec texture there is NONE. So with sr_direct_output=1, sr_mvec_decode=0: CreateFeature fails at view rect A, sr_feat.failed latches; if the view rect later changes while the quantized colour texture and output extents stay constant (a ScreenPercentage nudge within the same 4-pixel bucket), neither key fires and the whole pass stays SR_BAILed despite a render-extent change that feature_matches would treat as a different feature. The create-fail log's actual promise (dlss_sr.hpp:617, "retried when the colour-input or output extent moves") is honest; the comment's stronger claim is not.
fix: Correct the comment to state that a view-rect-only move at constant texture/output extents is NOT caught once create has failed in the direct+no-mvec configuration (or extend the coarse key to include render_w/render_h, recorded after the jitter read, if that narrow retry is wanted).

title: User-facing tooltips cite stale line numbers after the merges
failure_scenario: Three overlay tooltips (overlay_ui.hpp:2613, :3777, :3888) tell the user 'stray_dlssnr.cpp:4339-4341 declines to FreeLibrary even at device teardown'; :4339-4341 is now chain-mode motion-guide code - the real site is stray_dlssnr.cpp:7057. Similarly, code comments cite ':1816, :2043, :3307' as the three sites consulting codec_failed (all three now point at unrelated code), overlay_ui.hpp:2669 cites ':3206-3210' for pending_res recycling (now the view_discover_tries block), and overlay_ui.hpp:163 cites ':2640-2645'. A user or maintainer following these citations lands on the wrong mechanism, and the tooltip ones ship in the UI.
fix: Replace raw line-number citations in tooltips and comments with function names (nr_destroy_device, nr_update_clip_to_prev_clip, nr_ensure_output) which survive refactors; correct the three tooltip strings now.

title: init_complete's publication-order comment contradicts pd_create's actual code and the service's own reliance on it
failure_scenario: nr_state::init_complete's header says pd_create "PUBLISHES through set_private_data on its FIRST statement (descriptor_shadow.hpp:892-901), so nr_lazy_ngx_init hands this object to the whole process before it has initialised a single field of it". descriptor_shadow.hpp:894-901 shows the opposite order: `T *p = new T()` fully default-constructs every field (in-class initializers, atomics included) BEFORE set_private_data publishes the pointer. The in-flight branch of nr_service_reconfigure (:7250) depends on exactly that guarantee — "pending_work is safe to touch here ... a std::atomic that pd_create value-initialised BEFORE it published the pointer" — so the two comments assert opposite facts about the same call. Concrete: a reader trusting the init_complete comment concludes the service's `st_raw->pending_work.fetch_or(...)` on a not-yet-complete state races an unconstructed atomic and "fixes" it by dropping the re-queue — reintroducing the lost-reconfigure defect (bits drained and discarded during the arm window) that the in-flight branch was written to close.
fix: Correct the init_complete comment to say publication happens after default construction but before nr_lazy_ngx_init's ~25 field writes — which is the actual hazard the flag guards — so the two comments agree.

title: Stale counts: "ALL 33 OF THEM", "forty-one keys", and "TWO THINGS, NOT TEN" vs 62 owned keys and 4 relaunch rows
failure_scenario: The persistence header (:1512) says "EVERY KEY THE PANEL OWNS IS ROUND-TRIPPED, AND THAT IS NOW ALL 33 OF THEM" and the owned-field intro (:792) says "the list at forty-one keys" — OVERLAY_OWNED_FIELDS and owned_keys() both now carry 62 keys (33 was the pre-DLSS-SR count). The draw_load_only header (:3842-3845) says "IT IS TWO THINGS, NOT TEN ... These two remain" while the function draws FOUR relaunch-gated rows (app_id, require_trampoline 0->1, dlss_nr, dlss_sr 0->1) and the UI text itself says "These four are not"; the top-of-file ladder likewise still says "RELAUNCH-ONLY, AND ONLY THESE TWO". Concrete: a maintainer adding key #63 uses the stated count as the checklist invariant (the very drift the OWNED_FIELDS macro comment warns produces "a Save button that never lights up for it"), or a reviewer reconciling the header's "two" against the panel's "(4)" burns time deciding which is the bug.
fix: Replace the literal counts with references to the single source of truth (OVERLAY_OWNED_FIELDS / the draw_load_only rows), or update 33->62, forty-one->sixty-two, and two->four in the three comments.
